items.purpose: The change-control process says how anyone asks to change a Beacon baseline (scope, schedule, cost, data and classification, privacy or security controls, service levels), how the impact is assessed, who decides, and how the decision is recorded and passed on. The Programme Manager writes and runs it. The change-control board, chaired by Marcus Bell (E-002), approves the process and decides changes; the sponsor, Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001), decides anything that moves a gate or uses the management reserve. You set it up in week 2 with the RAID log and use it in week 7 to decide CR-01. It applies to all three releases, every time a baseline would move.

sections.heading: Scope and baselines
sections.guidance: List the baselines the process protects and the document that holds each one: scope statement, WBS and requirements; schedule gates; budget at completion and management reserve; classification and the privacy impact assessment; security acceptance criteria; service levels. Say what is not a change, such as fixing a defect against an agreed requirement. It is good when anyone can tell, for any request, whether it must come through change control.

sections.heading: Roles and the change-control board
sections.guidance: Name the chair, members, secretary, quorum and meeting rhythm, and write the decision authority as testable triggers: what the Programme Manager may approve alone, what needs the board, and what needs the sponsor (a gate moves, the reserve is used, a charter objective changes). Avoid words like minor and major. It is good when two people reading it would send the same request to the same decision maker.

sections.heading: Change request form
sections.guidance: Show the fields every request must fill in: ID, date, requester, the change asked for, the need behind it, the baselines it touches and urgency. Fill it in for a real request (CR-01) so the reader sees a complete example. A good form captures the need as well as the requested solution, because the board often meets the need another way.

sections.heading: Process steps and time targets
sections.guidance: Write the steps from raise to close as a numbered list, each with an owner and a time target: log, triage, assess, decide, update baselines, implement, verify and close. Include the link to the IT change process for changes to live systems. It is good when nothing can reach the build team before a recorded decision.

sections.heading: Impact assessment
sections.guidance: Compare at least two options across scope, schedule (critical path and float), cost (CPI and reserve), quality, risk, privacy under the Health Information Act, security and classification, and service support. Use real numbers from the schedule, register and data, not opinions. It is good when the decision almost writes itself from the table.

sections.heading: Decision record
sections.guidance: Record the decision, who decided and when, who was present, the rationale with the rule or evidence behind it, the impact accepted, any conditions and how the requester was told. A good record lets someone who missed the meeting explain the decision and check that its conditions were met.

sections.heading: Change log and baseline updates
sections.guidance: Keep one log of every request with its status, and list which documents change after each decision and which do not. It is good when every approved change can be traced to new document versions, and every rejected change still shows its reason.

## Scope and baselines

Use this process for any change to a Project Beacon baseline:

- Scope: scope statement (BCN-R1-05), work breakdown structure (BCN-R1-07), requirements register (BCN-R1-06).
- Schedule: gates in BCN-R1-08: Release 1 go-live 2026-10-23, Release 2 acceptance 2026-11-26, programme acceptance 2026-12-17.
- Cost: budget at completion (BAC) CAD 1,200,000; management reserve CAD 120,000, held by the sponsor.
- Information: data elements, classification (BCN-R1-13), privacy impact assessment (BCN-R1-14).
- Controls and service: security acceptance criteria (BCN-R1-18), service levels (BCN-R1-23).

Fixing a defect against an agreed requirement is not a change.

| Role | Who | Responsibility |

Decision authority (agreed):
- Programme Manager: no effect on a gate, cost inside the work package budget, no change to data, classification or controls.

## Process steps and time targets

1. Raise: the requester completes the form; the Programme Manager logs it within 1 working day.
2. Triage: the Programme Manager checks it and sets the authority level.
3. Assess: data, privacy, security and service leads complete the impact assessment within 5 working days.
4. Decide: the board or the sponsor decides and the secretary records it.
5. Update baselines: each owner updates and re-versions the affected documents.
6. Implement: live changes also need an IT change record in the IT Service Management Platform (A-011).
7. Verify and close: the requester confirms the result and the log is closed.

Assessing only schedule and cost. Every Beacon change must also be checked for privacy under the Health Information Act, classification and security, which is what decided CR-01.

Recording only 'rejected'. A useful decision record gives the rationale, the approved alternative, the conditions and which documents change.

items.purpose: The register lists every information asset Release 1 touches, from source systems to the dashboards, and gives each one a Kestrel classification (Public, Internal, Confidential or Restricted), a business owner, a system custodian, handling rules and a retention period. Tomás Rivera (E-006) maintains it as data steward; Priya Raman (E-003) and Daniel Osei (E-004) approve it; each owner confirms their rows. You build it in week 3 alongside the privacy impact assessment. It is checked at every design decision, export request and change request, such as CR-01.

sections.heading: Classification scheme
sections.guidance: Define Kestrel's four levels with a simple test for each and a Beacon example, and say which law governs which kind of information: the Health Information Act for patient health information, the Protection of Privacy Act for staff personal information. It is good when two people classify the same store the same way.

sections.heading: Information asset register
sections.guidance: One row per store of data: source systems, warehouse staging, de-identified views, the semantic model, service desk data, identity data, the exception table and the legacy Excel extracts. Give each an ID, the system ID, a class, a named owner and a named custodian. It is good when nothing that holds Kestrel data is missing and no owner is blank.

sections.heading: Reports and outputs
sections.guidance: Classify each report page, the app and exported files, name the sensitivity label and the audience, and state Kestrel's small-count rule. It is good when the label matches the class and the audience is a named group, not 'staff'.

sections.heading: Owners, stewards and custodians
sections.guidance: Explain each role in one line with a Beacon name. Separate Kestrel's legal role as custodian under the Health Information Act from the technical system custodian, and note affiliates such as consultants. It is good when it is clear who is accountable and who only operates the system.

sections.heading: Handling rules
sections.guidance: For each class, say where it may be stored, how it may be shared or sent, and whether it may be exported or printed, plus any vendor limits. Write rules a user can follow and a test can check. It is good when Restricted data has a clear 'never crosses' line.

sections.heading: Retention and disposal
sections.guidance: Give each asset a retention period, its source (Kestrel policy unless a law you can name sets it) and a disposal method with an owner. Include the retirement of the emailed extracts. It is good when every period can be checked and every disposal leaves a record.

sections.heading: Review and open issues
sections.guidance: Say when the register is reviewed and list open issues with an owner and a due date. It is good when known gaps, such as an unrecorded vendor or an excess grant, are visible rather than hidden.

## Classification scheme

Kestrel policy uses four levels. A store takes the class of the most sensitive item it holds.

| Level | Test | Release 1 example |
|---|---|---|
| Public | Anyone may see it | Site names and zones |
| Internal | Staff only; low harm if disclosed | Unit list, service desk tickets |
| Confidential | Named groups only; de-identified health data or staff personal information | Pseudonymous visit rows, bed census, dashboards |
| Restricted | Individually identifying health information | Clinical Information System (CIS) records, warehouse staging |

Patient health information falls under the Health Information Act (HIA). Staff records, such as identity data, are personal information under the Protection of Privacy Act (POPA).

## Information asset register

| ID | Asset | System | Class | Owner | Custodian |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IA-01 | Emergency visit times, triage level, disposition | A-002 Emergency Department Tracking Board | Restricted | E-007 | E-009 |
| IA-02 | Daily bed census by unit | A-006 Bed Management System | Restricted | E-008 | E-009 |
| IA-03 | Patient record | A-001 CIS | Restricted | E-001 | E-009 |
| IA-04 | Staging extracts | A-010 Clinical Data Warehouse | Restricted | E-006 | E-009 |
| IA-05 | De-identified views (khn_ed_visits, khn_bed_census) | A-010 | Confidential | E-007 (emergency view); E-008 (bed view) | E-009 |
| IA-06 | Beacon semantic model | A-009 Power BI service | Confidential | E-008 | E-006 |
| IA-07 | Service desk tickets | A-011 IT Service Management Platform | Internal | E-005 | E-009 |
| IA-08 | Data-quality exception table | A-010 | Confidential | E-006 | E-009 |
| IA-09 | Sign-in and site group membership | A-007 Identity Directory | Confidential | E-002 | E-009 |
| IA-10 | Legacy morning Excel extracts | A-013 Email and Collaboration | Restricted | E-008 | E-017 |

## Reports and outputs

| Output | Class and label | Audience |
|---|---|---|
| Executive overview page | Confidential | All-sites group: E-001, E-002, E-003, E-004, E-008, E-026 |
| Site operations pages (emergency flow, beds) | Confidential | Site groups, through the app as Viewers |
| Beacon app and semantic model | Confidential; label on the semantic model and each report (an app has no label of its own) | Named security groups only |
| Exports to Excel or PDF | Confidential; the label travels with Excel and PDF exports. CSV export is turned off, because labels are not applied to CSV files | Approved export group |

Kestrel reporting rule (policy, not law): suppress any count under 5, and blank any rate whose numerator is under 5, in any report shared outside the care team. Medians are not suppressed by this rule. Prairie Gate Health Centre (PGH) had 55 valid emergency visits from 1 July to 30 September 2026, so its small counts are tested first (R-02).

## Owners, stewards and custodians

- Under the HIA, Kestrel is the custodian of the health information. Employees and contractors, including Lumen Analytics Partners (V-05) staff, are affiliates and must follow Kestrel's privacy policies.
- Business owner: accountable for the asset; approves its use and access. Example: Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007) for emergency data.
- Data steward: Tomás Rivera (E-006) keeps definitions, quality rules and this register current.
- System custodian: runs and protects the system day to day. Kevin Park (E-009) is custodian of most sources and must not approve access to them (issue I-01).

## Handling rules

| Class | Store | Share and send | Export and print |
|---|---|---|---|
| Restricted | Source systems and A-010 staging only; never enters the Power BI service | Care team and named custodians; never by email | Not allowed from Beacon |
| Confidential | A-010 views and A-009 | Named groups through the app; Kestrel accounts only | Approved export group; label kept |
| Internal | Kestrel systems | Kestrel staff | For work use |
| Public | Anywhere | Anyone | Allowed |

Vendor access: V-05 build access is limited to Confidential data and ends with its contract on 2026-11-30 (R-07).

## Retention and disposal

| Asset | Retention (Kestrel policy, agreed) | Disposal |
|---|---|---|
| IA-01 to IA-03 | Unchanged by Beacon; Kestrel health records schedule | Source system owner |
| IA-04 staging | 30 days after each load reconciles | Logged purge job, E-009 |
| IA-05 and IA-06 | From 2026-07-01; rolling 24 months | Removed at refresh, E-006 |
| IA-08 exception table | Life of the service, as quality evidence (rule DQ-13) | Yearly review, E-006 |
| IA-10 legacy extracts | Stop at go-live, 2026-10-23 | Delete mailbox and share copies within 30 days; owners confirm |

## Review and open issues

The register is reviewed at every release gate and whenever a change request adds a data element.

| Issue | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|
| A-009 is vendor hosted but its provider is not in the vendor register | E-004 | 2026-10-16 |
| Power BI data region to be confirmed; HIA section 60 safeguards apply to any storage or use outside Alberta | E-003 | 2026-10-16 |
| E-009 holds provision, approve and audit-log rights (I-01) | E-002 | Release 2 |
| E-013 holds an excess "view all sites" grant on A-009 | E-006 | 2026-10-20 |
mistakes: Using 'custodian' loosely. Under the Health Information Act, Kestrel is the custodian; inside the register, the system custodian is the technical role. Mixing the two hides who is accountable.
Classifying everything Restricted to be safe, or classifying staging as Confidential because the dashboards are. Classify each store by what it actually holds so the controls match the risk.
Leaving out the emailed Excel extracts and the exception table. Anything that holds Kestrel data, including legacy copies and quarantined rows, needs a row, an owner and a retention rule.
Treating staff identity data as health information. It is personal information under the Protection of Privacy Act, with its own rules.

items.purpose: The privacy impact assessment describes how Release 1 collects, uses and discloses health information, how that could affect patients' privacy, and how Kestrel limits and protects the information. Under section 64 of the Health Information Act, Kestrel must prepare it and submit it to the Information and Privacy Commissioner for review and comment before the analytics system is implemented. The Commissioner reviews it and sends a closing letter with comments and recommendations; the Commissioner does not approve it. Tomás Rivera (E-006) and the Programme Manager write it, Priya Raman (E-003) approves it inside Kestrel, and Daniel Osei (E-004) reviews the safeguards. You write it in week 3 (schedule task 4, 2026-09-09 to 2026-09-24, on the critical path) and update it whenever a change adds or changes identifying health information.

sections.heading: Project description and need for an assessment
sections.guidance: Describe the system in plain words: where the data comes from, where identifying information sits, and what users see. Then say why an assessment is required: Kestrel is a custodian, and section 64 of the Health Information Act requires one for a new information system that relates to the collection, use and disclosure of individually identifying health information, submitted before implementation. It is good when a reader outside the project understands the system in one minute.

sections.heading: Information flow and data elements
sections.guidance: Number the flow steps and list every data element with where it is held and why it is needed. Show which identifiers are never extracted and which stay in staging. It is good when each element has a reason and anything without a reason has been removed.

sections.heading: Authority, purpose and minimization
sections.guidance: State the purpose, who confirmed the authority to use the information, and how the design meets sections 57 and 58 of the Health Information Act: the highest degree of anonymity (consider aggregate data first) and the least amount of information needed. Add Kestrel's small-count rule, labelled as policy. It is good when each design choice points back to one of these duties.

sections.heading: Safeguards
sections.guidance: List administrative, technical and physical safeguards with owners, as section 60 requires, and deal with storage or use outside Alberta. Describe any keep-data-in-Canada rule as Kestrel policy or contract, not law. It is good when every safeguard can be tested.

sections.heading: Privacy risks and mitigations
sections.guidance: Number each privacy risk, link it to the RAID log where it exists, give the mitigation and the residual rating. Use real Beacon facts such as the PGH visit count and the missed leavers. It is good when no risk is left without an owner or a planned action.

sections.heading: Breach response
sections.guidance: Explain what affiliates must do, and Kestrel's duty under section 60.1: where there is a risk of harm to an individual, notify the Commissioner as soon as practicable, and also the Minister responsible under the Act and the affected individuals, in writing to individuals. It is good when the steps and the decision maker are clear.

sections.heading: Approval, submission and updates
sections.guidance: Record internal approval, the security review, the submission date to the Commissioner for review and comment, the implementation date and how the closing letter will be handled. Say what changes trigger an update. It is good when the dates prove submission came before implementation and nobody claims the Commissioner approved it.

| Document ID | BCN-R1-14 |
| Title | Privacy impact assessment: Beacon patient-flow analytics (Release 1) |
| Prepared by | Tomás Rivera (E-006) and the Programme Manager |
| Internal approval | Priya Raman (E-003), Chief Privacy Officer |
| Version and date | 1.0, 2026-09-24 |
| Status | Approved inside Kestrel; submitted to the Information and Privacy Commissioner for review and comment, 2026-09-24 |

## Project description and need for an assessment

Release 1 replaces emailed morning Excel extracts with Power BI dashboards on emergency department flow and bed occupancy. Data moves from the Emergency Department Tracking Board (A-002) and the Bed Management System (A-006) into staging in the Clinical Data Warehouse (A-010), which holds individually identifying health information. De-identified views then feed the Beacon semantic model in the Power BI service (A-009).

Kestrel is a custodian under the Health Information Act (HIA). Section 64 requires a privacy impact assessment for a new information system relating to the collection, use and disclosure of individually identifying health information, submitted to the Commissioner before implementation.

## Information flow and data elements

1. A-002 and A-006 send visit times and daily unit census rows to A-010 staging (Restricted).
2. Staging creates a pseudonymous visit_id and an age band; the views drop the source identifiers (Confidential).
3. The data gateway refreshes the model from the views only.
4. Users see aggregated pages through the Beacon app, filtered by site with row-level security (RLS).

| Element | Where held | Why needed |
|---|---|---|
| Name, personal health number | Not extracted | Not needed |
| Birth date, source encounter number | Staging only | Derive age_band and visit_id; reconcile to source |
| visit_id (pseudonymous) | Views and model | Counts and de-duplication |
| Site, arrival, triage, physician initial assessment and departure times | Views and model | Waits and length of stay |
| Triage level, disposition, arrival mode, age band | Views and model | Acuity, patients who left without being seen, case mix |
| Unit census: staffed, occupied, alternate level of care (ALC) patients | Views and model, counts only | Occupancy and ALC days |

## Authority, purpose and minimization

- Purpose: manage emergency and inpatient flow at Kestrel's four sites and track the charter targets (agreed): median minutes to physician initial assessment at Kestrel General Hospital from 80.5 to 60; left-without-being-seen rate from 5.7% to 4.5%.
- Authority: confirmed by the Privacy Office for managing Kestrel's own services (legal review on file).
- Highest degree of anonymity (section 57): Kestrel first considered whether aggregate data is enough; for every Release 1 question it is.
- Least amount of information (section 58): only the elements above are extracted; names and health numbers never leave the source systems.
- Small counts: Kestrel policy is to suppress any count under 5, and blank any rate whose numerator is under 5, in reports shared outside the care team. Prairie Gate Health Centre (PGH), with 55 valid visits from 1 July to 30 September, is tested first (R-02).

## Safeguards

Section 60 requires reasonable administrative, technical and physical safeguards.

| Type | Safeguard | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Administrative | Privacy training before access; confidentiality terms for V-05 consultants, who are affiliates; quarterly access review | E-003, E-005 |
| Technical | Site RLS from Identity Directory (A-007) groups; readers are Viewers only | E-006 |
| Technical | Confidential label; export limited to a group; gateway reads the views only | E-004, E-009 |
| Physical | Warehouse in Kestrel's data centre; dashboards on Kestrel devices | E-002 |

Confirm the Power BI data region before go-live. If health information is stored or used outside Alberta, section 60 requires safeguards that protect its confidentiality there. Keeping data in Canada is Kestrel policy and contract, not a statute.

## Privacy risks and mitigations

| ID | Risk | Mitigation | Residual |
|---|---|---|---|
| P-01 | Small counts at PGH identify a patient (R-02) | Suppress counts under 5 and blank rates with a numerator under 5; age bands; tested in BCN-R1-21 | Low |
| P-02 | Visit-level rows exported and emailed | Export group; label; no names | Low |
| P-03 | A user sees another site's data | Site RLS, positive and negative tests | Low |
| P-04 | Missed leavers E-014 and E-027 still enabled (I-02) | Disable; named groups only; Release 2 leaver process | Medium |
| P-05 | V-05 access outlives its contract (2026-11-30, R-07) | Guest account expiry | Low |
| P-06 | Legacy extracts stay in mailboxes | Stop at go-live; delete within 30 days | Medium |
| P-07 | Activity logs processed in the United States by Sentinel SOC Services (V-04, R-05) | No forwarding until privacy review and contract terms | Medium |

## Breach response

An affiliate must tell Kestrel, the custodian (Kestrel policy: the Privacy Office, the same day). Under section 60.1, where there is a risk of harm to an individual from a loss or an unauthorized access or disclosure, Kestrel notifies the Information and Privacy Commissioner as soon as practicable, and also the Minister responsible under the Act and the affected individuals, in writing to individuals. The Privacy Office records the risk-of-harm decision.

## Approval, submission and updates

| Step | Who | Date |
|---|---|---|
| Internal approval; safeguards reviewed | Priya Raman (E-003); Daniel Osei (E-004) | 2026-09-24 |
| Submitted to the Commissioner for review and comment | Privacy Office | 2026-09-24 |
| Implementation (go-live) | Sponsor | 2026-10-23 |
| Closing letter: record comments and actions | Privacy Office | When received |

The Commissioner reviews and comments; it does not approve, and Kestrel stays accountable. If a change adds or changes identifying health information, such as a patient-level list on a dashboard, update this assessment and submit it before implementing.
mistakes: Writing that the Commissioner approved the assessment. Under the Health Information Act the Commissioner reviews and comments; Kestrel's Chief Privacy Officer approves it internally and Kestrel stays accountable.
Submitting after go-live. The assessment must be submitted before implementation, which is why its schedule task sits on the critical path.
Assessing only the dashboards. The identifying data sits in warehouse staging, so the flow from the source systems into staging needs the closest attention.

Calling a keep-data-in-Canada rule the law. No Alberta statute bans storage outside Canada; the Health Information Act requires safeguards for information stored or used outside Alberta, and Kestrel's own rule is policy or contract.

items.purpose: The workbook is the evidence of how Release 1 data was profiled and cleaned in Power Query: every problem found in the emergency department, bed census and service desk files, the Kestrel data-quality rule applied to it, the M code that applies the rule, the rows set aside, and the reconciliation that proves the cleaned tables match the approved figures. Mei Tanaka (E-013) builds it, Tomás Rivera (E-006) reviews it as data steward and owner of risk R-01, and the data owners (E-007, E-008, E-005) confirm the corrections to their data. You start it in week 1 with the emergency file and finish it in week 3; the quality plan, the model and every measure test depend on it.

sections.heading: Sources and rules
sections.guidance: Name each file, its period and its data owner, and the rule set you apply (Kestrel DQ-01 to DQ-14). Say that column profiling ran on the entire data set, because Power Query profiles only the first 1,000 rows by default. It is good when the reader knows exactly what was examined and against which rules.

sections.heading: Profiling summary
sections.guidance: Record what column quality, column distribution and column profile showed before any cleaning: distinct counts, empty values, errors after typing, and values outside the allowed list. It is good when every issue in the log can be traced to a profiling finding.

sections.heading: Issue log
sections.guidance: One row per problem: an ID, the exact row IDs, the problem, the rule and the handling. Cover every deliberate problem in the three files, including the ones you keep (flagged, not removed). It is good when someone could repeat your cleaning from the table alone.

sections.heading: Cleaning queries
sections.guidance: Show the M code with real file and column names: a staging query that types and flags rows, and a loaded fact query that references it, renames to target names and builds derived columns. Use a parameter for the folder. It is good when each rule in the log appears as a visible, named step.

sections.heading: Exception table
sections.guidance: Describe where quarantined rows go, which rule sent them there, and how errors are kept as evidence instead of deleted (DQ-13). It is good when every removed row can still be found and explained.

sections.heading: Reconciliation
sections.guidance: Compare your results with the approved figures: row balance for each file, counts by site and type, non-null derived columns and a few headline measures. It is good when every line matches, and any difference is explained by a rule, not adjusted by hand.

sections.heading: Sign-off and open actions

## Sources and rules

khn_ed_visits.csv (emergency department (ED) visits, 1 July to 30 September 2026, owner E-007), khn_bed_census.csv (midnight census by unit, owner E-008) and khn_service_desk.csv (tickets, August and September, owner E-005). Rules: Kestrel data-quality (DQ) rules DQ-01 to DQ-14. Profiling ran on the entire data set, not the first 1,000 rows.

## Profiling summary

- ED: 480 rows, 478 distinct visit_id; site_code 5 distinct (KGH, ARH, CVH, PGH, "kgh"); ctas_level 7 distinct (0 to 6); 1 error after typing arrival_datetime; departure_datetime empty once.
- Beds: 643 distinct unit-days, 644 expected; alc_patients minimum -1.
- Tickets: 219 distinct ticket_id in 220 rows; priority empty once; resolved_at empty 9 times (open tickets, normal).

## Issue log

| ID | Rows | Problem | Rule | Handling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ED-01 | V0315, V0318 | Exact duplicates | DQ-01 | Remove second copy |
| ED-02 | V0140, V0309 | site_code "kgh" | DQ-03 | Upper case; count for KGH |
| ED-03 | V0070 (6), V0222 (0) | ctas_level outside 1 to 5 | DQ-05 | Quarantine; E-007 corrects |
| ED-04 | V0385, V0421 | Physician initial assessment (PIA) before triage or arrival | DQ-06 | Keep; null MinutesToPIA and EDLOSMinutes |
| ED-05 | V0268 | No departure, not left without being seen (LWBS) | DQ-06 | Keep; null EDLOSMinutes |
| ED-06 | V0476 | Arrival 2026-09-31 does not exist | DQ-04 | Quarantine |
| ED-07 | V0075 | LWBS with a PIA time | DQ-07 | Quarantine |
| BC-01 | KGH-ICU 2026-07-15 | Exact duplicate | DQ-01 | Remove second copy |
| BC-02 | ARH-SUR 2026-08-16 | Missing unit-day | DQ-09 | Report to E-008; do not impute |
| BC-03 | KGH-MED4A 2026-09-08 | 34 occupied, 32 staffed | DQ-11 | Keep; OverCapacityFlag TRUE |
| BC-04 | CVH-MED 2026-07-22 | Alternate level of care (ALC) patients -1 | DQ-05 | ALCPatients null; keep beds |
| TK-01 | SD-10210 | Exact duplicate | DQ-01 | Remove second copy |
| TK-02 | SD-10089 | Resolved before opened | DQ-06 | Keep; ResolutionHours null; SLAMet blank |
| TK-03 | SD-10057 | Priority blank | DQ-02 | Keep; outside the service level agreement (SLA) measure |
| TK-04 | SD-10011 | sla_met Y at 77.3 hours, target 72 | DQ-08 | Recompute all flags; becomes N |

## Cleaning queries

stg_EDVisit (connection only) feeds FactEDVisit. SourceFolder is a parameter.

```
let
    Source = Csv.Document(File.Contents(SourceFolder & "khn_ed_visits.csv"), [Delimiter = ",", Encoding = 65001]),
    Promoted = Table.PromoteHeaders(Source, [PromoteAllScalars = true]),
    Deduped = Table.Distinct(Promoted),
    Blanks = Table.ReplaceValue(Deduped, "", null, Replacer.ReplaceValue, {"pia_datetime", "departure_datetime"}),
    Upper = Table.TransformColumns(Blanks, {{"site_code", each Text.Upper(Text.Trim(_)), type text}}),
    Raw = Table.AddColumn(Upper, "RawArrival", each [arrival_datetime], type text),
    Typed = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Raw, {{"arrival_datetime", type datetime}, {"triage_datetime", type datetime}, {"pia_datetime", type datetime}, {"departure_datetime", type datetime}, {"ctas_level", Int64.Type}}),
    Flagged = Table.AddColumn(Typed, "DQRule", each
        if (try [arrival_datetime])[HasError] then "DQ-04"
        else if [ctas_level] < 1 or [ctas_level] > 5 then "DQ-05"
        else if [disposition] = "LWBS" and [pia_datetime] <> null then "DQ-07"
        else null, type nullable text)
in
    Flagged
```

```
let
    Valid = Table.SelectRows(stg_EDVisit, each [DQRule] = null),
    Ordered = Table.AddColumn(Valid, "OrderOK", each [triage_datetime] >= [arrival_datetime]
        and ([pia_datetime] = null or [pia_datetime] >= [triage_datetime])
        and ([departure_datetime] = null or [departure_datetime] >= (if [pia_datetime] = null then [triage_datetime] else [pia_datetime])), type logical),
    PIA = Table.AddColumn(Ordered, "MinutesToPIA", each if [OrderOK] and [pia_datetime] <> null
        then Number.Round(Duration.TotalMinutes([pia_datetime] - [arrival_datetime])) else null, Int64.Type),
    LOS = Table.AddColumn(PIA, "EDLOSMinutes", each if [OrderOK] and [departure_datetime] <> null
        then Number.Round(Duration.TotalMinutes([departure_datetime] - [arrival_datetime])) else null, Int64.Type),
    ArrDate = Table.AddColumn(LOS, "ArrivalDate", each DateTime.Date([arrival_datetime]), type date),
    Renamed = Table.RenameColumns(ArrDate, {{"visit_id", "VisitID"}, {"site_code", "SiteCode"}, {"arrival_datetime", "ArrivalDateTime"}, {"ctas_level", "CTASLevel"}, {"triage_datetime", "TriageDateTime"}, {"pia_datetime", "PIADateTime"}, {"disposition", "Disposition"}, {"departure_datetime", "DepartureDateTime"}, {"age_band", "AgeBand"}, {"arrival_mode", "ArrivalMode"}}),
    Result = Table.RemoveColumns(Renamed, {"DQRule", "OrderOK", "RawArrival"})
in
    Result
```

## Exception table

ex_EDVisit references stg_EDVisit and keeps the four rows where DQRule is not null, with their rule ID and RawArrival, the arrival text copied before the type change.

```
let
    Quarantined = Table.SelectRows(stg_EDVisit, each [DQRule] <> null),
    Loadable = Table.ReplaceErrorValues(Quarantined, {{"arrival_datetime", null}})
in
    Loadable
```

Table.ReplaceErrorValues nulls only the typed arrival_datetime error for V0476 so the table loads; RawArrival still holds the original text, 2026-09-31 10:41, so the evidence stays in the model as well as in the source file. Rows are never deleted (DQ-13).

## Reconciliation

| Check | Approved figure | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ED row balance | 480 = 474 + 2 duplicates + 4 quarantined | Match |
| ED by site | KGH 213, ARH 105, CVH 101, PGH 55 | Match |
| MinutesToPIA; EDLOSMinutes non-null | 445; 471 | Match |
| Median minutes to PIA; LWBS | 64.0; 27 (5.7%) | Match |
| Bed row balance | 644 = 643 + 1; 1 unit-day missing | Match |
| ALC patient-days; average daily occupancy | 2,075; 87.0% | Match |
| Ticket row balance; types | 220 = 219 + 1; 113, 57, 49 | Match |
| SLA met | 137 of 212 (64.6%); 5 pending | Match |

## Sign-off and open actions

Reviewed by E-006, 2026-09-22. Open: E-007 to correct the triage level for V0070 and V0222; Tomás Rivera (E-006), as data steward, to resolve V0075 (LWBS with a PIA time, DQ-07) against the ED Tracking Board (A-002), with Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007) deciding the clinical meaning, left without being seen or assessed; E-008 to supply ARH-SUR 2026-08-16 and confirm KGH-MED4A 2026-09-08 and CVH-MED 2026-07-22; E-005 to fix SD-10089 times and set SD-10057 priority.
mistakes: Deleting bad rows instead of quarantining them. A removed row is lost evidence; Kestrel keeps quarantined rows in an exception table with the rule that sent them there.
Dropping out-of-order visits from the count. V0385 and V0421 are real visits; only their time measures are nulled, so they still count in visits and the LWBS rate.
Profiling on the default first 1,000 rows. Set profiling to the entire data set or rare problems, like the single invalid date, stay hidden.
Trusting the stored sla_met flag. Recompute it from the timestamps; SD-10011 says Y but took 77.3 hours against a 72-hour target.

items.purpose: The quality plan defines what good enough to release means for Release 1 and how it is proved: the quality gates for data, model, accuracy, performance, accessibility and security, the source-to-target and reconciliation controls, who tests and who accepts, the test methods and evidence, and the defect thresholds for go-live. The Programme Manager owns it, Tomás Rivera (E-006) and Mei Tanaka (E-013) run the data and model tests, and Janelle Cardinal (E-008) and Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007) accept the results. You write it in week 3 and record the test results in week 5; the go-live decision on 2026-10-23 rests on it.

sections.heading: Quality objectives and standards
sections.guidance: State the few standards every Release 1 output must meet, each in measurable words: figures reconcile to the approved figures, one definition per measure, no identifying data in the model, an accessibility standard and a performance target labelled as agreed. It is good when each objective can be tested and failed.

sections.heading: Roles
sections.guidance: Name who plans, who tests each area, who witnesses and who accepts. Separate builder and reviewer so nobody signs off their own work. It is good when every gate has a named tester and a named acceptor who did not build the thing.

sections.heading: Quality gates
sections.guidance: Give each gate an ID, the area, pass criteria and the evidence document. Cover data, model, accuracy, performance, accessibility and security. It is good when a gate result is pass or fail with evidence, never a judgment call made on the day.

sections.heading: Source-to-target and reconciliation controls
sections.guidance: Explain how each target column is traced to its source rule and checked, then list the controls that run after each refresh: row balance per file, key matching against dimensions, and headline measures against the approved figures. It is good when the expected values are written down before testing starts.

sections.heading: Test methods and evidence
sections.guidance: Say how each kind of test is done (DAX query view, Performance Analyzer, keyboard and screen-reader checks, View as and Test as role, the app) and what counts as evidence. Include a sample test query. It is good when another tester could repeat the test and get the same result.

sections.heading: Defects and acceptance thresholds
sections.guidance: Define defect severities and how many of each are allowed at go-live. Wrong figures and privacy or security failures must allow none. It is good when the threshold is agreed with the acceptors before testing, not negotiated after.

sections.heading: Results at the go-live gate
sections.guidance: Record each gate's result with its date and any condition. Show open items honestly, with the decision that covers them. It is good when the go-live decision can be read straight from this table.

## Quality objectives and standards

- Every published figure matches the approved reconciliation figures after rounding to the displayed precision.
- One definition per measure, recorded in the Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) catalogue (BCN-R1-20).
- No individually identifying health information in the model; counts under 5 suppressed and rates whose numerator is under 5 blanked on shared pages (Kestrel policy).
- Every page meets Kestrel's accessibility standard, Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 level AA.
- Every visual renders in 3 seconds or less in Performance Analyzer (agreed target).

## Roles

| Role | Who |
|---|---|
| Quality owner | Programme Manager |
| Data and model tests | Tomás Rivera (E-006), Mei Tanaka (E-013) |
| Security and access tests | Sam Okafor (E-020), privacy tests witnessed by Priya Raman (E-003) |
| Support readiness | Grace Liu (E-005) |
| Acceptance | Janelle Cardinal (E-008), Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007) |

Nobody signs off their own work: E-013 tests the measures E-006 wrote, and E-006 reviews the queries E-013 built.

## Quality gates

| Gate | Area | Pass criteria | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| QG-1 | Data | Row balance holds for every file; every issue has a rule and an owner | BCN-R1-15 |
| QG-2 | Model | Star schema as designed; DimDate marked; single-direction one-to-many relationships; 0 unmatched keys | BCN-R1-19 |
| QG-3 | Accuracy | Every catalogue measure matches its expected result, overall, by site and by triage level | BCN-R1-20 test log |
| QG-4 | Performance | Every visual renders in 3 seconds or less in Performance Analyzer, in Desktop and in the service | Performance Analyzer export |
| QG-5 | Accessibility | Text contrast at least 4.5:1; alt text on every visual; tab order set; meaning never by colour alone; usable by keyboard and screen reader | Accessibility checklist |
| QG-6 | Security | Row-level security (RLS) positive and negative tests pass; small counts suppressed; Confidential label applied; workspace roles as designed | BCN-R1-21, BCN-R1-18 |

## Source-to-target and reconciliation controls

Each target column in source-to-target.csv carries a rule and a reconciliation check. These controls run after every refresh during testing. ED is the emergency department, PIA the physician initial assessment, LWBS left without being seen and SLA service level agreement.

| Control | Expected |
|---|---|
| ED row balance | 480 source = 474 loaded + 2 duplicates + 4 quarantined |
| Bed row balance | 644 = 643 + 1 duplicate; 1 missing unit-day reported |
| Ticket row balance | 220 = 219 + 1 duplicate |
| Keys | 0 unmatched SiteCode, UnitID or CTASLevel; every fact date found in DimDate (365 rows, 2026) |
| Headline measures | ED Visits 474; Median Minutes to PIA 64.0; LWBS Rate 5.7%; Occupancy % (Average Daily) 87.0%; SLA Met % 64.6% |

## Test methods and evidence

- Accuracy: run test queries in DAX query view and compare with the expected tables. Example, expected ARH 105, 54.5, 4.8%; CVH 101, 54.0, 4.0%; KGH 213, 80.5, 7.5%; PGH 55, 45.5, 3.6%:

```
EVALUATE
SUMMARIZECOLUMNS (
    DimSite[SiteCode],
    "ED Visits", [ED Visits],
    "Median Minutes to PIA", [Median Minutes to PIA],
    "LWBS Rate", [LWBS Rate]
)
ORDER BY DimSite[SiteCode]
```

- Performance: Performance Analyzer on each page after Refresh visuals; slow visuals re-run as queries in DAX query view.
- Accessibility: keyboard-only and screen-reader walk-through of each page, plus the contrast check.
- Security: View as role in Power BI Desktop, Test as role in the service, then real test accounts through the app.
- Evidence: test ID, date, tester and result, filed with the gate. A test without evidence counts as not run.

## Defects and acceptance thresholds

| Severity | Meaning | Allowed at go-live |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Wrong figure, privacy or security failure | None |
| 2 | Function fails with no workaround | None |
| 3 | Fails with a workaround | Up to 3, each with an owner and date |
| 4 | Cosmetic | Logged for the improvement register |

## Results at the go-live gate

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| QG-1 Data | Pass, 2026-10-20; owner corrections still open are handled by rule |
| QG-2 Model | Pass, 2026-10-15 |
| QG-3 Accuracy | Pass, 2026-10-20; all expected results matched |
| QG-4 Performance | Pass, 2026-10-21 |
| QG-5 Accessibility | Pass, 2026-10-21 |
| QG-6 Security | Pass except small-count suppression for Prairie Gate Health Centre (PGH), which became go-live condition D-02 on 2026-10-23; verified the same day in BCN-R1-21 |
mistakes: Writing objectives such as 'accurate dashboards' with no pass criteria. Each gate needs a measurable test and named evidence, such as 474 valid visits and a 64.0-minute median.
Letting builders accept their own work. Separate the builder from the tester, and have the business owners accept the results.
Testing performance and security only in Power BI Desktop. Both behave differently in the service and through the app, so test there too.
Treating a missing result as a pass. No evidence means the test was not run, and the gate cannot pass.

items.purpose: The threat model and architecture shows how emergency and bed data travel from the clinical systems to the Power BI service and its users, where the data crosses trust boundaries, what could go wrong at each step (using STRIDE), which controls stop or detect it, and the residual risk with its owner. Daniel Osei (E-004) owns it, Sam Okafor (E-020) and Tomás Rivera (E-006) help build it, Priya Raman (E-003) reviews the privacy side and Janelle Cardinal (E-008) accepts it as business owner. You build it in week 3 (schedule task 7, 2026-09-09 to 2026-09-17). The security acceptance criteria and the RLS test pack then prove it.

sections.heading: Components and data flows
sections.guidance: Number every flow from source to user and give its source, destination, data, classification and protection in transit. Include vendor access as a flow. It is good when nothing moves between systems without a numbered flow.

sections.heading: Trust boundaries
sections.guidance: Name each boundary, the flows that cross it, and what must be true at the crossing (what data may cross, which account, which check). It is good when each boundary has a rule a tester can check.

sections.heading: Classification and handling by zone
sections.guidance: Say the highest class allowed in each zone and the labels and reporting rules that apply. It is good when it matches the classification register exactly.

sections.heading: Controls
sections.guidance: List preventive, detective and corrective controls with where they sit and who owns them. It is good when each control maps to at least one misuse case and has an owner who will produce evidence.

sections.heading: Misuse cases (STRIDE)
sections.guidance: Write realistic misuse cases for Beacon, tag each with a STRIDE category (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege), name the control and the concern that remains. Use real findings from the data. It is good when every STRIDE category is considered and residual concerns are specific.

sections.heading: Residual risk register
sections.guidance: For each significant risk give the inherent and residual rating, the owner and the decision (accept, treat, transfer, avoid), using the RAID log IDs. It is good when every risk above Kestrel's appetite has a decision by the accountable executive, advised by the Chief Information Security Officer.

sections.heading: Sign-off
sections.guidance: Record the security review, the privacy review with the privacy impact assessment reference, and business owner acceptance, with dates. It is good when the people who own the risks are the people who signed.

| Owner | Daniel Osei (E-004), Chief Information Security Officer |

## Components and data flows

| Flow | From | To | Data and class | Protection |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Emergency Department Tracking Board (A-002) | Clinical Data Warehouse (A-010) staging | Visit times, triage level, disposition; Restricted | Transport Layer Security (TLS); read-only extract account |
| F2 | Bed Management System (A-006) | A-010 staging | Daily unit census; Restricted | As F1 |
| F3 | A-010 staging | A-010 de-identified views | Pseudonymous visit_id, age band; Confidential | Inside the warehouse; views under change control |
| F4 | A-010 views | Gateway, then Power BI service (A-009) | Scheduled refresh; Confidential | Gateway makes outbound TLS connections only |
| F5 | A-009 | Users | Pages filtered by row-level security (RLS); Confidential | TLS; Kestrel sign-in |
| F6 | Identity Directory (A-007) | A-009 | Sign-in and group membership | Directory synchronization over TLS |
| F7 | Lumen Analytics Partners (V-05) | Beacon workspace | Build access; Confidential | Named guest accounts expiring 2026-11-30 |

## Trust boundaries

| Boundary | Between | Flows | What must be true |
|---|---|---|---|
| TB1 | Clinical systems and analytics zone | F1, F2 | Only data-dictionary fields plus encounter number and birth date cross; extract accounts read-only and logged |
| TB2 | Kestrel network and Power BI cloud | F4, F6 | Restricted data never crosses; the gateway account reads the views only |
| TB3 | Power BI service and user devices | F5 | Kestrel sign-in; readers are Viewers under RLS; Confidential label; export limited |
| TB4 | Kestrel and third parties | F7; Sentinel SOC Services (V-04) | Named, time-limited vendor access; no logs to V-04 in the United States until the R-05 privacy review is done |

## Classification and handling by zone

- Clinical systems and A-010 staging: Restricted; stays on premises.
- A-010 views and A-009: Confidential at most; Confidential sensitivity label on the semantic model and every report in the app.
- Shared pages: counts under 5 suppressed and rates whose numerator is under 5 blanked (Kestrel policy); Prairie Gate Health Centre (PGH) is tested first.

## Controls

| Control | Type | Where | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| De-identification in views | Preventive | A-010 | E-006 |
| Small-count suppression measures | Preventive | A-009 | E-006 |
| Site RLS from A-007 groups | Preventive | A-009 | E-006 |
| Readers get Viewer or app access only | Preventive | A-009 | E-006 |
| Confidential label; export limited to a group | Preventive | A-009 | E-003, E-004 |
| Gateway account read-only on views | Preventive | Gateway, A-010 | E-009 |
| Activity and audit logs reviewed weekly | Detective | A-009, A-007 | E-020 |
| Quarterly review of workspace and RLS membership | Detective | A-009 | E-005 |
| Refresh failure alerts the service desk (Analytics Support) within 1 hour; data-as-of time on each page | Detective | A-009 | E-006 |
| Restore of warehouse and model from backup | Corrective | A-010, Backup Platform (A-012) | E-016 |

## Misuse cases (STRIDE)

| Misuse case | STRIDE | Control | Residual concern |
|---|---|---|---|
| A Member-role analyst sees every site, because RLS does not filter people who can edit | Information disclosure | Only named builders hold Admin, Member or Contributor | E-013 holds an excess "view all sites" grant; remove it |
| A user exports visit-level rows and emails them | Information disclosure | Export group; label; no names in the model | Screenshots remain possible |
| Someone identifies a patient from a count of 1 to 4 at PGH | Information disclosure | Suppression; age bands | Must be proven before go-live (BCN-R1-21) |
| A stolen gateway credential reads staging | Spoofing | No staging rights for that account; log review | Low |
| A missed leaver opens the app: E-014 and E-027 are still enabled (I-02) | Spoofing | App audience is named groups; disable both | Leaver automation arrives in Release 2 |
| V-05 keeps access after its contract | Elevation of privilege | Guest expiry 2026-11-30; exit checklist (R-07) | Low |
| A view is changed to expose an identifier | Tampering | Change control and peer review of views | Low |
| A measure change cannot be traced to a person | Repudiation | Activity log; version history | Low |
| A refresh fails silently and leaders act on stale numbers | Denial of service | Alerts to E-006 and the desk; data-as-of time | Medium until monitoring is automated |

## Residual risk register

| Risk | Inherent | Residual | Owner | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-02 Small counts at PGH | High | Low | Priya Raman (E-003) | Treat: suppression, tested |
| R-05 Logs processed in the United States by V-04 | High | Medium | Priya Raman (E-003) | Treat: no forwarding until review and contract safeguards |
| Missed leavers reach the app (I-02) | High | Medium | Daniel Osei (E-004) | Treat now; accepted until the Release 2 gate by Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001) |
| R-07 V-05 contract ends 2026-11-30 | Medium | Low | Programme Manager | Treat: expiry and handover |
| Stolen gateway credential | Medium | Low | Daniel Osei (E-004) | Accept |

## Sign-off

- Security architecture reviewed: Daniel Osei (E-004), 2026-09-17.
- Privacy review: Priya Raman (E-003); privacy impact assessment BCN-R1-14.
- Business owner acceptance: Janelle Cardinal (E-008), 2026-09-17.
mistakes: Drawing boxes without numbered flows. Each flow needs its data, classification and protection, or you cannot say what crosses each trust boundary.
Assuming RLS protects everyone. It filters Viewers and app users only; anyone with Admin, Member or Contributor on the workspace sees every site.
Listing controls with no owner or evidence. Every control needs an owner and a matching test in the security acceptance criteria.
Leaving residual risk unowned. Above Kestrel's appetite it needs a recorded decision by the accountable executive, advised by the Chief Information Security Officer.

items.purpose: Security acceptance criteria turn the privacy impact assessment and the threat model into conditions that someone other than the builder can observe and test before go-live. Each criterion states what must be true, how it is checked, who owns it, and its status at the gate. Daniel Osei (E-004) owns the document, Priya Raman (E-003) owns the privacy criteria, Sam Okafor (E-020) and Tomás Rivera (E-006) run the checks, and the go-live gate on 2026-10-23 decides on them. You write them in week 3 with the threat model and record their status in week 5.

sections.heading: Scope and how the criteria are used
sections.guidance: Say which components the criteria cover, that each is pass or fail, who may check it, how it traces to the threat model, and what happens at the gate if one is not met. It is good when the rule for go-live is written before testing starts.

sections.heading: Privacy criteria
sections.guidance: Write criteria for the privacy impact assessment submission, the absence of identifiers in the model and small-count suppression, each with the check and owner. Use real expected values. It is good when a criterion names the numbers a tester should see.

sections.heading: Access criteria
sections.guidance: Cover site row-level security, workspace roles, excess grants, missed leavers and vendor expiry. It is good when each criterion names the accounts or groups involved, not 'appropriate users'.

sections.heading: Data protection and platform criteria
sections.guidance: Cover the sensitivity label, export limits and the gateway account's rights, including a negative check (what must be refused). It is good when at least one check proves something is blocked.

sections.heading: Monitoring and recovery criteria
sections.guidance: Cover log review, refresh failure alerts and the ability to restore the service within its recovery time objective. It is good when each criterion is tested by forcing the failure in a test environment.

sections.heading: Status at the go-live gate
sections.guidance: Record the status of every criterion on the gate date with its evidence. Show anything not met as a condition or an exception, never by deleting it. It is good when the table matches the go-live decision exactly.

sections.heading: Exceptions and accepted risk
sections.guidance: List criteria deliberately left to a later release, with the baseline, who accepted the risk, who advised and the end date. It is good when every exception expires on a named date.

items.purpose: The star schema and relationship design defines the Beacon semantic model: the fact tables and the grain of each, the dimensions that describe them, keys, relationships, cardinality and filter direction, the date design, column properties and storage mode, plus the checks that prove the model behaves as designed. Tomás Rivera (E-006) writes it and builds the model, and Mei Tanaka (E-013) reviews it. Every measure, the RLS roles and every report page depend on it. You design it in week 4 and confirm it when you build the date table and relationships.

sections.heading: Business questions and scope
sections.guidance: List the questions the model must answer, in the leaders' words. They decide which facts and dimensions you need and which you leave out. It is good when every table in the model serves at least one question.

sections.heading: Fact tables and grain
sections.guidance: For each fact, write its grain as 'one row per ...', its type (transaction or periodic snapshot), its row count after cleaning and how its numbers add up. It is good when nobody could put two different grains in one table, and semi-additive columns are named.

sections.heading: Dimension tables
sections.guidance: Give each dimension its key, row count and attributes, and explain any snowflake. It is good when each key is unique and every attribute users filter on lives in a dimension, not a fact.

sections.heading: Relationships and filter direction
sections.guidance: List every relationship with its one side, many side, cardinality, cross-filter direction and whether it is active. Explain why you avoid bidirectional filters and how you would handle a second date on the same fact. It is good when the table matches the model view exactly.

sections.heading: Date design
sections.guidance: Describe the one shared date table: its range (full calendar year), how it is built, that it is marked as the date table, and the role it plays for each fact. It is good when classic time intelligence will work and no fact needs its own date table.

sections.heading: Column properties and storage mode
sections.guidance: Choose Import, DirectQuery or Direct Lake with a reason, and record hidden columns, sort-by columns, summarization and where measures live. It is good when report authors see only what they should use.

sections.heading: Validation
sections.guidance: Record the checks that prove the design: unmatched keys, dimension row counts, fact dates found in the date table and a filtered result compared with the approved figures. It is good when each check has an expected value from the data and a result.

| Title | Star schema and relationship design: Beacon semantic model |
| Owner | Tomás Rivera (E-006), Clinical Analytics Lead |
| Reviewer | Mei Tanaka (E-013), Clinical Analyst |
| Version and date | 1.0, 2026-10-08 |
| Status | Approved |

## Business questions and scope

- How long do patients wait from arrival to physician initial assessment (PIA), by site and Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale (CTAS) level?
- How many patients leave without being seen (LWBS)?
- What is the emergency department (ED) length of stay (LOS) for admitted and discharged patients?
- How full are the units on the last day and on average, and how many alternate level of care (ALC) patient-days are there?
- Are service desk tickets resolved within target?

## Fact tables and grain

| Fact | Grain: one row per | Type | Rows | How it adds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FactEDVisit | Valid ED visit | Transaction | 474 | Counts add; times use medians |
| FactBedCensus | Unit per census date (midnight) | Periodic snapshot | 643 | Semi-additive: add across units, never across dates |
| FactServiceTicket | Service desk ticket | Transaction | 219 | Counts add |

MinutesToPIA and EDLOSMinutes are built in Power Query and are null where the source times are missing or out of order.

## Dimension tables

| Dimension | Key | Rows | Attributes |
|---|---|---|---|
| DimDate | Date | 365 (2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31) | Year, MonthNumber, MonthName, DayOfWeek |
| DimSite | SiteCode | 4 | SiteName, Zone, SiteType |
| DimUnit | UnitID | 7 | SiteCode, UnitName, UnitType |
| DimCTAS | CTASLevel | 5 | CTASDescription, TargetMinutes |

DimUnit relates to DimSite, a small snowflake. It lets a site filter, and the site row-level security (RLS) role, reach the bed census through the unit.

## Relationships and filter direction

| One side | Many side | Cardinality | Cross-filter | Active |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DimDate[Date] | FactEDVisit[ArrivalDate] | One to many | Single | Yes |
| DimDate[Date] | FactBedCensus[CensusDate] | One to many | Single | Yes |
| DimDate[Date] | FactServiceTicket[OpenedDate] | One to many | Single | Yes |
| DimSite[SiteCode] | FactEDVisit[SiteCode] | One to many | Single | Yes |
| DimSite[SiteCode] | FactServiceTicket[SiteCode] | One to many | Single | Yes |
| DimSite[SiteCode] | DimUnit[SiteCode] | One to many | Single | Yes |
| DimUnit[UnitID] | FactBedCensus[UnitID] | One to many | Single | Yes |
| DimCTAS[CTASLevel] | FactEDVisit[CTASLevel] | One to many | Single | Yes |

No bidirectional filters: they create ambiguous paths and could let a fact filter a dimension around the site role. Ticket analysis by resolved date is out of scope. If it is needed, add ResolvedDate with an inactive relationship to DimDate and switch to it inside a measure with USERELATIONSHIP.

## Date design

One shared DimDate, generated in Power Query for the full calendar year 2026 and marked as the date table on Date. It is contiguous, so classic time intelligence works; calendar-based time intelligence also exists but is still in preview. DimDate plays three roles, arrival date, census date and opened date, through one relationship to each fact, with no copies. The code is in BCN-R1-20.

## Column properties and storage mode

- Storage mode: Import. The de-identified views are small and refresh daily through the gateway, and Import gives the fastest visuals. DirectQuery adds load on the warehouse for no benefit, and Direct Lake needs Delta tables in Microsoft Fabric OneLake, such as a lakehouse or warehouse, which Beacon does not use.
- Hide the fact-side keys and dates (SiteCode, UnitID, CTASLevel, ArrivalDate, CensusDate, OpenedDate) so users filter through dimensions.
- MonthName sorts by MonthNumber. Keys, MinutesToPIA and EDLOSMinutes are set to Don't summarize.
- Measures live in a separate measure table, named exactly as in BCN-R1-20.
- Column formats: dates as yyyy-mm-dd; percentages to one decimal place.

## Validation

| Check | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Unmatched SiteCode in FactEDVisit and FactServiceTicket | 0 | 0 |
| DimUnit sites missing from DimSite | 0 | 0 |
| Fact dates missing from DimDate | 0 (ED arrivals 2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30) | 0 |
| Dimension rows | DimDate 365, DimSite 4, DimUnit 7, DimCTAS 5 | Match |
| Filter DimSite to KGH | ED Visits 213; Occupancy % (Average Daily) 89.3%; Tickets 110 | Match |
| No filter | ED Visits 474; Tickets 219; Staffed Beds (Last Snapshot) 144 | Match |
mistakes: Mixing grains in one fact table, such as adding the daily census to the visit rows. Each fact gets its own declared grain.
Summing staffed beds across dates. FactBedCensus is a snapshot: 12,952 staffed bed-days over the quarter is not 144 beds.
Turning on bidirectional filtering to make one visual work. It creates ambiguous paths and can let filters slip around the site role; fix the measure or the design instead.
Building a date table that only covers the data months. Use a contiguous full calendar year, marked as the date table, so time intelligence and future data work.

items.purpose: The date table and DAX catalogue is the single reference for every measure in the Beacon semantic model: its business definition, its exact Data Analysis Expressions (DAX), how blanks and small counts behave, and its tested result compared with the approved figures. It also holds the Power Query code for DimDate and the rule for marking it as the date table. Tomás Rivera (E-006) writes the measures, Mei Tanaka (E-013) tests them, and the business owners of each figure, Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007), Janelle Cardinal (E-008) and Grace Liu (E-005), agree the definitions. You build it in week 4. Any new or changed measure, such as those for CR-01, is added here and tested before it is published.

sections.heading: Date table
sections.guidance: Show the Power Query code that builds a contiguous full-year DimDate, its row count, the sort-by column and the mark-as-date-table step. It is good when the table has no gaps, so classic time intelligence works.

sections.heading: Measure conventions
sections.guidance: State the shared rules: where measures live, how they are named, why medians are used for times, how nulls are left out, and how snapshot data is handled. It is good when a new measure can be written to the same pattern without asking anyone.

sections.heading: Emergency department measures
sections.guidance: Give the exact DAX for visits, time to physician initial assessment, percent within the CTAS target, LWBS rate and length of stay. It is good when each formula matches the Kestrel definition and uses the real table and column names.

sections.heading: Bed census measures
sections.guidance: Give the DAX for average daily and last-snapshot occupancy, staffed beds and ALC measures, and explain why beds are never added across dates. It is good when the semi-additive behaviour is visible in the code.

sections.heading: Service desk measures
sections.guidance: Give the DAX for tickets, SLA met percent and median access request days, saying which tickets are left out and why. It is good when the denominator rule is explicit.

sections.heading: Shared-page and time-intelligence measures
sections.guidance: Give the measures that apply Kestrel's small-count rule on shared pages and at least one classic time-intelligence measure. It is good when suppression returns blank, not zero, for empty combinations so visuals do not fill with fake rows.

sections.heading: Test results
sections.guidance: Table every measure with its definition and its tested result against the approved figures, plus where by-site results are recorded. It is good when every expected value comes from the reconciliation figures and every result says whether it matched.

| Status | Approved; every result matches |

## Date table

DimDate covers the full year 2026 (365 rows) and is marked as the date table on Date, which checks the dates are unique, never blank and contiguous. MonthName sorts by MonthNumber.

```
let
    StartDate = #date(2026, 1, 1),
    EndDate = #date(2026, 12, 31),
    Dates = List.Dates(StartDate, Duration.Days(EndDate - StartDate) + 1, #duration(1, 0, 0, 0)),
    AsTable = Table.FromList(Dates, Splitter.SplitByNothing(), {"Date"}),
    Typed = Table.TransformColumnTypes(AsTable, {{"Date", type date}}),
    AddYear = Table.AddColumn(Typed, "Year", each Date.Year([Date]), Int64.Type),
    AddMonthNumber = Table.AddColumn(AddYear, "MonthNumber", each Date.Month([Date]), Int64.Type),
    AddMonthName = Table.AddColumn(AddMonthNumber, "MonthName", each Date.MonthName([Date]), type text),
    AddDayOfWeek = Table.AddColumn(AddMonthName, "DayOfWeek", each Date.DayOfWeekName([Date]), type text)
in
    AddDayOfWeek
```

## Measure conventions

- Measures live in one measure table, named as below. ED is emergency department, PIA physician initial assessment, CTAS the Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale, LWBS left without being seen, LOS length of stay, ALC alternate level of care, SLA service level agreement.
- Times use medians, because a few very long stays pull an average up.
- Null MinutesToPIA and EDLOSMinutes rows (missing or out-of-order times) are left out on purpose.
- Bed measures add across units on one date, never across dates.
- Small-count rule (Kestrel policy) for pages shared outside the care team: counts under 5 show as "<5" and rates whose numerator is under 5 show blank. A total that would let a reader work out a suppressed cell by subtraction is suppressed too, with ED Visits (Shared Total) below (tested in BCN-R1-21, SUP-07). Medians are not suppressed by this rule. Shared measures return text or blank, never a mix of text and numbers, so text measures go in tables, matrices and cards and charts use numeric measures that return blank.

## Emergency department measures

```
ED Visits = COUNTROWS ( FactEDVisit )

Median Minutes to PIA =
MEDIANX ( FILTER ( FactEDVisit, NOT ISBLANK ( FactEDVisit[MinutesToPIA] ) ), FactEDVisit[MinutesToPIA] )

% PIA Within CTAS Target =
DIVIDE (
    COUNTROWS ( FILTER ( FactEDVisit, NOT ISBLANK ( FactEDVisit[MinutesToPIA] )
        && FactEDVisit[MinutesToPIA] <= RELATED ( DimCTAS[TargetMinutes] ) ) ),
    COUNTROWS ( FILTER ( FactEDVisit, NOT ISBLANK ( FactEDVisit[MinutesToPIA] ) ) )
)

LWBS Rate = DIVIDE ( CALCULATE ( [ED Visits], FactEDVisit[Disposition] = "LWBS" ), [ED Visits] )

Median ED LOS Hours =
DIVIDE ( MEDIANX ( FILTER ( FactEDVisit, NOT ISBLANK ( FactEDVisit[EDLOSMinutes] ) ), FactEDVisit[EDLOSMinutes] ), 60 )

Median ED LOS Hours Admitted = CALCULATE ( [Median ED LOS Hours], FactEDVisit[Disposition] = "Admitted" )

Median ED LOS Hours Discharged = CALCULATE ( [Median ED LOS Hours], FactEDVisit[Disposition] = "Discharged" )
```

## Bed census measures

```
Occupancy % (Average Daily) =
AVERAGEX (
    FILTER ( VALUES ( DimDate[Date] ), CALCULATE ( SUM ( FactBedCensus[StaffedBeds] ) ) > 0 ),
    DIVIDE ( CALCULATE ( SUM ( FactBedCensus[OccupiedBeds] ) ), CALCULATE ( SUM ( FactBedCensus[StaffedBeds] ) ) )
)

Occupancy % (Last Snapshot) =
VAR LastCensusDate = MAX ( FactBedCensus[CensusDate] )
RETURN CALCULATE ( DIVIDE ( SUM ( FactBedCensus[OccupiedBeds] ), SUM ( FactBedCensus[StaffedBeds] ) ), DimDate[Date] = LastCensusDate )

Staffed Beds (Last Snapshot) =
VAR LastCensusDate = MAX ( FactBedCensus[CensusDate] )
RETURN CALCULATE ( SUM ( FactBedCensus[StaffedBeds] ), DimDate[Date] = LastCensusDate )

ALC Days = SUM ( FactBedCensus[ALCPatients] )

ALC Patients (Last Snapshot) =
VAR LastCensusDate = MAX ( FactBedCensus[CensusDate] )
RETURN CALCULATE ( SUM ( FactBedCensus[ALCPatients] ), DimDate[Date] = LastCensusDate )
```

The FILTER in the average skips calendar dates with no census rows, such as every date outside July to September.

## Service desk measures

```
Tickets = COUNTROWS ( FactServiceTicket )

SLA Met % =
DIVIDE (
    CALCULATE ( [Tickets], FactServiceTicket[SLAMet] = "Y" ),
    CALCULATE ( [Tickets], FactServiceTicket[SLAMet] IN { "Y", "N" } )
)

Median Access Request Days =
DIVIDE (
    CALCULATE (
        MEDIANX ( FILTER ( FactServiceTicket, NOT ISBLANK ( FactServiceTicket[ResolutionHours] ) ), FactServiceTicket[ResolutionHours] ),
        FactServiceTicket[TicketType] = "Access request"
    ),
    24
)
```

## Shared-page and time-intelligence measures

```
ED Visits (Shared) =
VAR Visits = [ED Visits]
RETURN IF ( ISBLANK ( Visits ), BLANK (), IF ( Visits < 5, "<5", FORMAT ( Visits, "#,0" ) ) )

LWBS Rate (Shared) =
VAR LWBSVisits = CALCULATE ( [ED Visits], FactEDVisit[Disposition] = "LWBS" )
RETURN IF ( LWBSVisits < 5, BLANK (), [LWBS Rate] )

ED Visits (Shared Total) =
VAR SmallSites =
    COUNTROWS (
        FILTER ( VALUES ( DimSite[SiteCode] ), [ED Visits] >= 1 && [ED Visits] <= 4 )
    )
RETURN
    IF (
        ISINSCOPE ( DimSite[SiteCode] ),
        [ED Visits (Shared)],
        IF ( SmallSites > 0, BLANK (), [ED Visits (Shared)] )
    )

ED Visits Previous Month = CALCULATE ( [ED Visits], PREVIOUSMONTH ( DimDate[Date] ) )
```

ED Visits (Shared Total) is for any shared matrix or table that shows a total across sites, with DimSite[SiteCode] on the rows. On a site row ISINSCOPE is true, so it shows the same as ED Visits (Shared). On the total row it checks every site in the filter, and if any has 1 to 4 visits it returns blank: in the matrix of admitted visits by site, KGH 31, ARH 15, CVH 9 and PGH "<5" show and the total of 59 is blank, so PGH's 4 cannot be worked out by subtraction. With no small site the total shows, for example 474 for all visits. It returns text or blank, like ED Visits (Shared). It protects totals across sites only, so a shared matrix does not add a second grouping with subtotals, such as disposition, without the same check.

## Test results

| Measure | Definition | Tested result, all sites |
|---|---|---|
| ED Visits | Valid visits | 474 |
| Median Minutes to PIA | Median arrival to PIA | 64.0 |
| % PIA Within CTAS Target | PIA at or under the level's target | 28.3% (126 of 445) |
| LWBS Rate | LWBS visits / visits | 5.7% |
| Median ED LOS Hours | Median arrival to departure | 3.82 |
| Admitted / Discharged | Same, by disposition | 11.96 / 3.61 |
| Occupancy % (Average Daily) | Average of daily occupied / staffed | 87.0% |
| Occupancy % (Last Snapshot) | Occupied / staffed on 2026-09-30 | 84.0% (121 of 144) |
| Staffed Beds (Last Snapshot) | Staffed beds on the last date | 144 |
| ALC Days | Sum of daily ALC patients | 2,075 |
| ALC Patients (Last Snapshot) | ALC patients on the last date | 21 |
| Tickets | Unique tickets | 219 |
| SLA Met % | Y / (Y + N), recomputed flags | 64.6% (137 of 212) |
| Median Access Request Days | Median resolution hours / 24 | 4.26 |
| ED Visits Previous Month | Visits in the prior month | 169 in September |
| ED Visits (Shared) | "<5" under 5 | Prairie Gate (PGH) LWBS shows "<5" |
| LWBS Rate (Shared) | Blank under 5 LWBS | KGH 7.5%, ARH 4.8%; CVH, PGH blank |
| ED Visits (Shared Total) | As ED Visits (Shared); a total across sites is blank when any site in the filter has 1 to 4 | Admitted by site: 31, 15, 9, "<5", total blank (SUP-07); all visits by site: total 474 |

By-site expected results are tested in the RLS test pack (BCN-R1-21).
mistakes: Averaging occupancy across all rows or summing staffed beds over days. Occupancy is semi-additive: work out each day first, then average the daily ratios.
Using AVERAGE for waits. A few very long stays pull the average up; Kestrel reports medians, such as 64.0 minutes to physician initial assessment.
Counting LWBS visits as misses in the percent within CTAS target. They have no assessment time, so they are outside the denominator of 445.
Making a suppression measure return '<5' for empty combinations. Return blank when there are no rows, or every visual fills with rows for dates and units that have no data.

items.purpose: The RLS test pack proves that row-level security in the Beacon semantic model shows each site only its own data, that people outside the roles see nothing, and that small counts are suppressed on shared pages. It holds the role design, test accounts and methods, positive and negative tests with expected results from the approved figures, the execution record and the sign-off. Tomás Rivera (E-006) configures the roles, Sam Okafor (E-020) runs the tests and Priya Raman (E-003) witnesses the privacy tests. Decision D-02 approved go-live on 2026-10-23 on one condition: small-count suppression for Prairie Gate Health Centre verified in this pack. You build it in week 4 and run it in week 5.

sections.heading: Role design
sections.guidance: Name each role, its DAX filter, the table it filters, the security group that supplies members and an example member. Explain how the filter reaches each fact and who RLS does not apply to. It is good when membership comes from groups, never from individual names typed into roles.

sections.heading: Test accounts and methods
sections.guidance: List the three ways you test (View as in Desktop, Test as role in the service, real accounts through the app) and why each is needed. It is good when at least one test uses the real app and real group membership.

sections.heading: Positive tests
sections.guidance: For each role, give the expected values of key measures from the approved figures and the actual result. It is good when the site figures add back to the all-sites figures.

sections.heading: Negative tests
sections.guidance: Test what must not happen: another site's data, no role, a missed leaver, two roles at once, drillthrough and builders who bypass RLS. It is good when each test states the expected refusal or blank.

sections.heading: Small-count suppression tests (D-02)
sections.guidance: Test Kestrel's rule with real small counts from the data, including the boundary at exactly 5, a zero, and a total that could reveal a suppressed cell by subtraction. It is good when each test shows the underlying count and the expected display.

sections.heading: Execution record and defects

sections.heading: Sign-off and retest triggers
sections.guidance: Record who tested, who witnessed and who accepted, and list the changes that require the pack to run again. It is good when the triggers are specific enough that the service desk and change board will catch them.
