## Role design

Each role filters DimSite with a Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) rule, one role per site: Kestrel General Hospital (KGH), Aspen Ridge Hospital (ARH), Coulee Valley Hospital (CVH) and Prairie Gate Health Centre (PGH). The filter flows to FactEDVisit and FactServiceTicket, and through DimUnit to FactBedCensus. Members come from Identity Directory (A-007) security groups.

| Role | DAX filter on DimSite | Group | Example member |
|---|---|---|---|
| Site KGH | [SiteCode] = "KGH" | BCN-RLS-KGH | Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007) |
| Site ARH | [SiteCode] = "ARH" | BCN-RLS-ARH | Dr. Liam O'Connor (E-012) |
| Site CVH | [SiteCode] = "CVH" | BCN-RLS-CVH | Dr. Ethan Wright (E-029) |
| Site PGH | [SiteCode] = "PGH" | BCN-RLS-PGH | Dr. Victor Leblanc (E-041) |
| All sites | TRUE () | BCN-RLS-ALL | Janelle Cardinal (E-008) |

RLS applies to Viewers and app users only. Workspace Admin, Member and Contributor see every site, so only named builders hold those roles.

## Test accounts and methods

1. Power BI Desktop: View as each role, before publishing.
2. Power BI service: Test as role on the semantic model's security page, as each role and as a named member.
3. The Beacon app: sign in with a test account in each group and open the executive and site pages. Only this step tests real group membership and the app audience.

## Positive tests

ED is emergency department and PIA is physician initial assessment. Expected values are the approved figures.

| Test | Role | ED Visits | Median Minutes to PIA | Occupancy % (Average Daily) | Tickets |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RLS-01 | Site KGH | 213 | 80.5 | 89.3% | 110 |
| RLS-02 | Site ARH | 105 | 54.5 | 84.8% | 43 |
| RLS-03 | Site CVH | 101 | 54.0 | 87.9% | 42 |
| RLS-04 | Site PGH | 55 | 45.5 | 76.8% | 24 |
| RLS-05 | All sites | 474 | 64.0 | 87.0% | 219 |

Staffed Beds (Last Snapshot) was also checked: KGH 72, ARH 40, CVH 22, PGH 10, all sites 144. Actual matched expected in every cell, and the four sites add back to 474 visits and 219 tickets.

## Negative tests

| Test | Action | Expected and actual |
|---|---|---|
| RLS-06 | Site KGH user tries to pick ARH | Site slicer lists KGH only; no ARH rows |
| RLS-07 | Site PGH user opens the bed page | Only PGH-MED appears |
| RLS-08 | Viewer in no role opens the app | No data shown |
| RLS-09 | Missed leavers E-014 and E-027 (I-02) checked against groups and app audience | In none of them |
| RLS-10 | User in both Site KGH and Site ARH | 318 visits (213 + 105): roles add together |
| RLS-11 | Site ARH user drills through from a chart | Detail page shows ARH only |
| RLS-12 | Mei Tanaka (E-013): Contributor in Beacon Dev only; Viewer in Site CVH in the Beacon Prod app, tries to choose all sites | Beacon Dev (de-identified test views): all sites, because RLS does not filter Contributors. Beacon app: CVH rows only, so the all-sites view is refused. Excess "view all sites" grant removed (SAC-06) |

## Small-count suppression tests (D-02)

Kestrel policy suppresses any count under 5, and blanks any rate whose numerator is under 5, on pages shared outside the care team. A total that would let a reader work out a suppressed cell by subtraction is suppressed too, and so is any other total on the page that would rebuild it. Medians are not suppressed. PGH is tested first because its counts are smallest. Counts come from the cleaned data, 1 July to 30 September 2026.

| Test | Check | Underlying count | Expected display |
|---|---|---|---|
| SUP-01 | PGH left without being seen (LWBS) | 2 | "<5"; LWBS Rate (Shared) blank |
| SUP-02 | PGH admitted visits | 4 | "<5" |
| SUP-03 | PGH triage level 5 visits | 6 | 6 |
| SUP-04 | PGH busiest day, 2026-07-18 | 5 | 5 (5 is not under 5) |
| SUP-05 | CVH LWBS visits | 4 | "<5"; LWBS Rate (Shared) blank |
| SUP-06 | PGH triage level 1 visits | 0 | Blank |
| SUP-07 | Executive page matrix of admitted visits by site, with a total | KGH 31, ARH 15, CVH 9, PGH 4; total 59, and 59 - 31 - 15 - 9 = 4 | PGH "<5"; the admitted total blank (ED Visits (Shared Total), BCN-R1-20), and no other total on the page lets a reader rebuild 59 |

## Execution record and defects

| Run | Date | Tests | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-10-20 | RLS-01 to RLS-12 | All passed |
| 2 | 2026-10-23 | SUP-01 to SUP-07 | All passed; witnessed by E-003 |

No defects are open.

## Sign-off and retest triggers

- Tested by Sam Okafor (E-020); D-02 condition verified by Priya Raman (E-003), 2026-10-23.
- Accepted for the business by Janelle Cardinal (E-008).
- Run the whole pack again after any change to roles, groups, DimSite, DimUnit or relationships, after any new measure that counts patients, and at each quarterly access review.
mistakes: Testing only that each site sees its own numbers. Negative tests (no role, wrong site, two roles, drillthrough) are what prove the boundary holds.
Relying on View as in Power BI Desktop. It does not test workspace roles, the app audience or real group membership, so repeat the tests in the service and the app.
Forgetting that RLS does not filter Admin, Member or Contributor. A builder seeing every site is expected, so keep those roles to named people.
Writing 'suppression works' without numbers. Show the underlying count, the expected display, the boundary at exactly 5, and a total that could give a suppressed cell away by subtraction.

items.purpose: The service value proposition says who the Beacon patient-flow analytics service is for, the outcomes it helps them achieve, what it provides (utility and warranty), the costs and risks it removes and introduces, how provider and consumers create value together, and how value will be measured. It is the ITIL basis for the service catalogue entry and service levels. The Programme Manager writes it with Grace Liu (E-005), the service owner; Janelle Cardinal (E-008), the business owner, and the sponsor, Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001), agree it. You write it in week 4 before the catalogue entry, and revisit it at each service review.

sections.heading: Service and consumers
sections.guidance: Describe the service in one sentence, then name the sponsor, customer and users, and the provider roles. It is good when every consumer role has a real Kestrel name or group, not 'the business'.

sections.heading: Problem and desired outcomes
sections.guidance: State the consumers' problem in their words and the outcomes they want, using data baselines and agreed targets. Separate outputs (dashboards) from outcomes (better decisions). It is good when each outcome could be measured.

sections.heading: Utility and warranty
sections.guidance: Utility is what the service does (fit for purpose); warranty is how well it does it (fit for use: availability, capacity, security, continuity). List both with Beacon specifics and label agreed targets. It is good when warranty items are measurable.

sections.heading: Costs and risks
sections.guidance: Show which costs and risks the service removes for consumers and which it introduces, with RAID log IDs and budget figures from the data. It is good when the introduced side is honest, not empty.

sections.heading: Value co-creation and the service relationship
sections.guidance: Explain what the provider contributes, what the consumers contribute, how feedback flows and how often the relationship is reviewed. It is good when consumers' own actions appear, because value is created together.

sections.heading: Four dimensions
sections.guidance: Check the service against the four dimensions: Organizations and People; Information and Technology; Partners and Suppliers; Value Streams and Processes. It is good when each answer names something concrete in Beacon.

sections.heading: Measures of value and review
sections.guidance: Give the measures, baselines, targets and timing, and say where the service sits in the product and service lifecycle. It is good when the baseline comes from data and the target is labelled as agreed.

## Service and consumers

The service gives Kestrel's emergency and patient-flow leaders one trusted, de-identified view of emergency department (ED) flow and bed pressure through the Beacon app in the Power BI service (A-009), supported by the service desk.

| Consumer or provider role | Who |
|---|---|
| Sponsor: authorizes and funds | Dr. Helen Marchetti (E-001) |
| Customer: sets requirements, owns outcomes | Janelle Cardinal (E-008); Dr. Sarah Whitford (E-007) for emergency data |
| Users | Site physicians (E-007, E-012, E-029, E-036, E-041), patient-flow leaders, executives |
| Provider | Tomás Rivera (E-006), model and data; Grace Liu (E-005), support |

## Problem and desired outcomes

Leaders work from Excel extracts emailed each morning. The numbers disagree between sites, nobody trusts them, and they carry more patient detail than anyone needs. The outcomes they want:

- Act on waits sooner: median minutes from arrival to physician initial assessment (PIA) at Kestrel General Hospital (KGH) from 80.5 to 60 (agreed target).
- Fewer patients left without being seen (LWBS): 5.7% to 4.5% across all sites (agreed target).
- Run the daily bed meeting from one set of numbers. From July to September 2026, average daily occupancy was 87.0%, and alternate level of care (ALC) patients used 2,075 patient-days, 18.4% of occupied bed-days.
- Stop arguing about whose number is right.

The dashboards are outputs. The outcome is earlier, better patient-flow decisions.

## Utility and warranty

| Utility: fit for purpose | Warranty: fit for use |
|---|---|
| Waits by site and Canadian Triage and Acuity Scale (CTAS) level; % within the CTAS target (28.3%, July to September) | Scheduled refresh daily at 05:00, so pages show yesterday's data by 06:00; a failed refresh alerts the service desk (Analytics Support) within 1 hour; data-as-of time on every page (agreed) |
| LWBS, ED length of stay, occupancy and ALC days | Recovery time objective 72 hours and recovery point objective 24 hours for A-009 (asset register) |
| Executive and site operations pages | De-identified, Confidential label, site row-level security, counts under 5 suppressed and rates with a numerator under 5 blanked |
| One governed definition per measure | Support through the service desk |

## Costs and risks

| | Removed for consumers | Introduced |
|---|---|---|
| Costs | Building and reconciling morning extracts by hand | Release 1 budget CAD 420,000; licences and support effort; time to learn the pages |
| Risks | Patient detail sent by email; decisions on numbers that disagree | Small counts at Prairie Gate Health Centre (R-02); key-person dependency on Tomás Rivera (R-06); Lumen Analytics Partners (V-05) contract ends 2026-11-30 (R-07); stale data if a refresh fails |

## Value co-creation and the service relationship

The provider supplies the model, the pages and support. Consumers supply clean source data and use the pages in their decisions: Dr. Sarah Whitford corrects the two invalid triage levels (V0070, V0222); Janelle Cardinal runs the bed meeting from the bed page; users report problems through the service desk. In August and September 2026 the desk logged 27 Power BI tickets, and their satisfaction score (CSAT) averaged 3.0 from 9 responses, against 3.5 for the whole desk. A monthly service review with Janelle Cardinal and Grace Liu checks the measures below.

## Four dimensions

| Dimension | Beacon answer |
|---|---|
| Organizations and People | Named owners; data steward E-006; service desk trained; Mei Tanaka (E-013) shares model knowledge to reduce R-06 |
| Information and Technology | De-identified views in A-010; model and app in A-009; sign-in from A-007 |
| Partners and Suppliers | V-05 build support until 2026-11-30; the Power BI provider to be added to the vendor register |
| Value Streams and Processes | Source data, warehouse, refresh, publish, use at the bed meeting, support, improve |

## Measures of value and review

| Measure | Baseline (data) | Target | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| Median minutes to PIA, KGH | 80.5 | 60 (agreed) | 2027-01-25, three months after go-live |
| LWBS rate, all sites | 5.7% | 4.5% (agreed) | 2027-01-25, three months after go-live |
| Power BI ticket CSAT | 3.0 (9 responses) | Set at the first service review | Monthly |
| Leaders using the app each week | New measure | Set at the first service review | Monthly |

On 2026-10-16 the service is in the Build stage of the ITIL product and service lifecycle, with Transition work (testing and service desk readiness) starting. The go-live gate on 2026-10-23 completes Transition into live use; from then the service is operated, delivered and supported (the Operate, Deliver and Support stages). Improvements go to the continual-improvement register (BCN-R1-28).
mistakes: Describing the dashboards instead of the outcomes. Leaders want earlier decisions and fewer patients leaving without being seen; the pages are only the output.
Listing only benefits. A value proposition also states the costs and risks the service introduces, such as R-02, R-06 and the end of the V-05 contract.
Leaving consumers out of value co-creation. Clean source data from the owners and real use of the pages at the bed meeting are part of how value is created.
Setting targets with no baseline. Use the data baselines (80.5 minutes, 5.7%) and label the targets as agreed with the sponsor.
